seed_question: Does economic inequality harm social cohesion?
sh_prerun_probe_claims: Economic inequality can lead to increased social tensions and conflicts.
Higher levels of inequality are correlated with lower levels of trust among citizens.
Communities with greater economic disparity often experience reduced civic participation.
Economic inequality can exacerbate disparities in access to education and healthcare.
Regions with high inequality may experience higher crime rates and social unrest.
Social cohesion is typically stronger in societies with more equitable income distribution.
Economic inequality can lead to feelings of disenfranchisement and marginalization.
Inequality can undermine democratic processes by concentrating political power among the wealthy.
Economic disparities can erode shared cultural and social values within a society.
Reducing economic inequality is associated with improved social mobility and inclusivity.
